title: Tech Billionaire Peter Thiel Breaks Ranks with Trump Over Iran Conflict
snippet: In leaked audio from a private lecture, top GOP mega-donor Peter Thiel criticized the U.S. military intervention in Iran, warning the nation could lose both hard and soft power.
content:
Silicon Valley billionaire and high-profile conservative donor Peter Thiel has publicly expressed deep skepticism over the Trump administration's military campaign in Iran, declaring that the U.S. "should not have done it."

Audio recorded at a private October 12 event in Nashville and obtained by POLITICO reveals a rare foreign policy rift between the tech mogul and President Donald Trump, coming just weeks before critical midterm elections.

A Fractured Stance on Foreign Policy

Addressing an audience during a lecture series, Thiel took direct aim at the decision to initiate military action in the Middle East. "I'm skeptical of [the war], I think we should not have done it," Thiel said. "There were a lot of mistakes that were made."

The Palantir co-founder further warned of broader strategic consequences for American global dominance. "Maybe we don't have the hard power. Maybe we're going to lose the soft power war," he added.

Targeting Neocons and International Courts

Despite his harsh critique of the Iran intervention, Thiel maintained his personal support for Trump, framing his comments as an effort to protect the president from neoconservative influences. In his remarks, Thiel heavily criticized traditional foreign policy hawks and speculated on the international legal ramifications facing the administration.

Thiel suggested that potential arrest warrants from the International Criminal Court (ICC) represent a "sword of Damocles hanging over the Trump administration as it tries to prosecute this war in Iran." He also dismissed criticisms from prominent Bush-era Republicans, characterizing anti-Trump stances from families like the Cheneys as attempts to curry favor with international courts.

Additionally, Thiel reflected on an early 2024 meeting with Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu following the October 7 attacks. According to Thiel, when pressed on military strategy in Gaza, Netanyahu remarked, "I can't just Dresdenize it," referencing the Allied firebombing of Dresden during World War II.

Broader Implications for the GOP

As Trump's earliest major Silicon Valley backer in 2016 and a key financial force behind Vice President JD Vance's 2022 Senate run, Thiel's pushback highlights growing fault lines within the populist right regarding foreign intervention. Neither representatives for Thiel nor the White House immediately issued statements regarding the leaked audio.
